title: Is folic acid good for everyone?
authors: Smith AD, Kim YI, Refsum H
funder: not stated in the abstract page read; full text not accessible
result: Critical review. When fortification is introduced, several hundred thousand people are exposed to more folic acid for each neural tube defect pregnancy prevented. The authors list possible harms: in animals, folic acid-rich diets alter DNA and histone methylation with phenotypic changes in later generations; in humans, raised unmetabolised folic acid, possibly lower natural killer cell cytotoxicity, a possibly reduced response to antifolate drugs for malaria, rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and cancer, cognitive impairment and anaemia with high folate and low B12 in older people, insulin resistance and obesity in children of mothers with that combination, and facilitated progression of preneoplastic lesions and subclinical cancers. They advise nations considering fortification to be cautious and to fund research on its effects.
